extracted.intended_audience: Navy claimants/major-sub-claimants, OPNAV-443, base commanders, contracting officers (KOs), Contracting Officer's Technical Representatives (COTRs), Quality Assurance Evaluators (QAEs) and contract administration staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for implementing the Department of the Navy's Commercial Activities (CA) program, focusing on pre-award cost comparison, post-award contract administration, quality assurance, performance definition (PWS), mobilization readiness, cost accounting, training, and contract type selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized claimant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for centralized guidance at the claimant level throughout the CA process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include: staff CA Program implementation offices with sufficient personnel (at least two), form field CA implementation teams to provide on-site assistance at key milestones (writing the PWS, forming the MEO, conducting the cost comparison), publish periodic 'Lessons Learned' synopses and submit recaps to OPNAV-443, and convene command meetings 60–90 days prior to transition to ensure command-level support and highlight problem areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Current instructions focus on pre-award activity; there is a need for systematic post-award direction on contract administration and dealing with performance problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: claimants publish Quality Assurance Manuals (containing sampling techniques, sample checklists, measurement issues), establish QAE training courses or obtain quotas, OPNAV-443 issue an instruction addressing post-award conversion issues and contingency options, streamline procedures for bringing temporary government employees and contractors onboard, and establish a central contingency fund to assist commands during resolicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance implementation and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequate QA inspections and documentation are essential; lack of QA documentation undermines enforcement of contract standards and jeopardizes litigation position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns: commands without QA plans or with poorly documented inspections cannot assess deductions or correct performance problems, often leading to termination/resolicitation. Guidance: implement QA plans early, maintain proper documentation, use sampling/checklists as in a QA manual, and invest in QA oversight to detect and correct problems early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence, experience, and training of QA personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: A competent, experienced, well-trained cadre of QA personnel is required to ensure PWS standards are met and to support enforcement actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in resources for guidance and training on QA, consider centralized guidance at CNO or major claimant level, provide QAE training courses/quotas, and ensure instructors have real-life CA experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance definition and PWS adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The adequacy of contractor performance is substantially determined by the clarity and completeness of the Performance Work Statement (PWS); complex operations are especially difficult to define.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems arise from workload variation, technology change, and mix/type of services. Recommendations: conduct audits/research on complex operations, possibly exclude some complex operations from the CA inventory, fund additional resources for PWS preparation during cost comparison, develop CA functional experts at claimant level to assist in PWS development, publish lists of commands and proven PWSs by functional area, and sequence reviews from simple to complex to build expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of sufficient resources for PWS development
rubrics_metrics.description: Most commands do not allocate sufficient resources for initial formulation of the PWS, resulting in poorly written or incomplete PWSs and subsequent performance problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider funding additional resources during the cost comparison process specifically for PWS preparation; invest in automation or other efficiency programs where appropriate; develop claimant-level experts to support PWS drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilization readiness and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor performance under mobilization is a concern; installations should plan to ensure contractor readiness for wartime or emergency mobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: require a mobilization contingency plan as part of the original contract with periodic updates, delineate mobilization requirements in solicitations, include mobilization clauses in contracts, require contractors to plan for recall of former military personnel, conduct periodic mobilization drills with contractors, and include contractors in mobilization planning and exercises where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of contract administration cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial cost comparisons routinely underestimate contract administration (CA) costs; actual CA costs frequently exceed the 4–6% (or 4–8%) ranges used in cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed practice: commands that invested more in CA staffing had smoother transitions and better performance. Recommendations: closer monitoring of CA administration costs through improved cost control/accounting systems, reassess OMB staffing standards (which may be too low), and negotiate QA staffing where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate cost accounting systems and cost 'yardsticks'
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing financial systems do not capture costs by CA function, making development of estimates and comparisons of estimated vs actual costs difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop better cost yardsticks for evaluating CAs after a decision, structure accounting systems to capture costs by function post-award, adjust estimates when underlying assumptions (wage rates, scope, period) change, and implement control systems to monitor post-award costs (Chapter V discusses recommendations for a control system).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and appropriateness of standard cost factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of standard cost factors (e.g., government retirement and fringe benefits) can distort cost estimates; current CA factor (27.05%) differs substantially from the 16–17% used elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate rationale for differing factors, research the reasons for variation, and avoid indiscriminate use of averages that may inflate some operations and deflate others; additional research and possible standardization recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of contracting out on budget flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractual obligations reduce local managerial budget flexibility during periods of budget cuts because contracts represent legal obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: activities with large contracted functions may be unable to reprogram funds, forcing critical missions to absorb cuts or shifting reductions across the claimancy. CNO should provide guidance on alternatives for dealing with funding reductions for activities with large multi-function contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract type selection for complex operations (procurement method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of procurement (sealed bid vs negotiated) and contract form affect quality of performance and flexibility; negotiated procurement is preferable for complex operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on data, negotiated procurement (two-step) should be the only procurement allowed for complex operations to better define requirements and manage change. Evaluate differences in administration costs and performance under different contract forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract form choice: Cost Plus Award Fee vs Firm Fixed Price
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract form affects documentation burden and incentives; Cost Plus Award Fee contracts may have less documentation requirement for award fees and can be used to streamline QA/incentivize performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider closer cost analysis comparing true contract administration costs and performance differences under Firm Fixed Price vs Cost Plus Award Fee. Note: award fee aspect is not subject to the Disputes Clause, reducing documentation requirements where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multi-function (umbrella/BOS) contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-function contracts (BOS) appear to produce better and smoother operations than multiple single-function contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: single contractor focal point, higher corporate oversight, economies of scale in solicitation/administration, single government SCM focal point, simpler customer complaint handling, and potentially better mobilization coordination. Recommendation: consider combining small single-function contracts into multi-function contracts where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training adequacy for CA program stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a need for more comprehensive, better publicized, and more accessible training on the CA program for CA implementation staff, KOs, COTRs, and QAEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues: limited course quotas (e.g., NAVFAC), some instructors lack real CA experience, attrition reduces expertise in some claimancies. Recommendations: expand number and variety of courses, provide specialized KO training for CA procurements, obtain quotas for QAE training, and ensure instructors have real-life CA experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring post-award events and program evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring of post-award events and costs is loosely structured, hindering objective assessment of program success and claimed cost savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without formal post-award control systems and reliable accounting data, pre-award estimates can be misstated and anecdotal evidence can be exaggerated. Implement formal post-award monitoring/control systems and maintain activity cost data in forms useful for program management to substantiate success/failure claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning and central contingency funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands often lack practicable options when contractors fail (default/bankruptcy); bringing temporary government employees or temporary contractors onboard is time-consuming and costly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: OPNAV-443 should issue instructions outlining options for dealing with contractor performance problems (including contingency plan formation and streamlined recruiting/detailing), establish a central contingency fund to assist commands in assembling contingency operations until resolicitation is complete, and publicize streamlined procedures for temporary staffing/contractors.
